summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said up front the task was bounded ("Bounded task… a short design in chat, no spec file"). It asked one clarifying question through AskUserQuestion: does the max length include the '...'? I picked the recommended answer. It then compared hard-cut vs word-boundary truncation in chat, recommended word boundary with a hard-cut fallback, and asked "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." After I approved, it wrote the tests first, then implemented and ran them. The only files written in the repo were format.js and format.test.js, and no docs/ directory was created.
reasoning: All seven criteria are met, and I checked each against the session log and the files on disk. Brainstorming was loaded before any coding. Claude announced the task as bounded, discussed both alternatives in chat and waited for approval. It wrote no spec file (no docs/ directory exists), and it started implementing after approval. The empty Codex result is an extra issue for the engineers to look at, but it didn't block the scenario.

observations.description: The Codex approach gate misbehaved. Codex preflight returned 'ok', but the one-shot approach call came back empty. Claude reported: "the one-shot approach call came back with an empty payload — no approaches… not retried." This may be because the seeded Codex is only a stub, but it's worth checking why preflight passes and the call then returns nothing.

Before presenting the two approaches, Claude asked an extra question (does the max length include the ellipsis?) through a multiple-choice prompt. It's a reasonable question, but it adds a round trip to a small task.
Claude corrected itself partway through. It first said truncate would compose with prefix/suffix "applied afterward", then said that was backwards and truncate must run last.

The design message recommended a hybrid (word boundary with a hard-cut fallback) instead of simply picking one of the two options the user offered. It still explained why each pure option falls short.

While testing, Claude noted two existing problems in the fixture and left them alone: the tests print a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning, and console.assert failures still end with "All tests passed".
Launch had several dialogs where the highlighted default was 'No, exit' (the trust-folder and bypass-permissions prompts), so each one needed Down+Enter to continue.
The design phase took about 2 minutes ("Baked for 2m 5s"), mostly on the Codex handoff, which returned nothing.

criteria.evidence: Session log 698eb0c2-….jsonl: the first tool_use is `Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`, which comes before any Edit or Write to format.js.
Assistant text in the log: "Bounded task — the flow already exists in `format.js`, and this is a choice between algorithms inside it. So: a short design in chat, no spec file."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired: both alternatives presented in chat and approval asked before coding
criteria.evidence: Chat message: "The reason the pure hard cut loses: … 'The quick b...'" and "The reason the pure word boundary loses: a single long token … bare '...'". Recommendation: "truncate at the last word boundary, falling back to a hard cut". It ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." There were no Edit calls to format.js before my approval.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls docs` in the workdir returned "No such file or directory". I listed every Write/Edit path in the log: two scratch files under ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/…/ (approach-context.md, approach-prompt.md), plus format.test.js and format.js. `git status --short` shows only ` M format.js` and ` M format.test.js`.
The only classification announced was "Bounded task". `grep -ci spike` on the session log found 1 matching line, which looks like the skill's own text. No assistant message calls the task a spike.

criteria.criterion: Did not classify as architectural or write a spec
criteria.evidence: Claude explicitly said "no spec file". The design stayed in chat, and no docs/ directory exists.

After "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the log shows Edits to format.test.js and format.js, then `node format.test.js` ("RED confirmed — 4 assertions fail" followed by a passing run). Final screen: "Done. Truncation at the last word boundary, with a hard-cut fallback."
